concepts.name: NHB: Establishment, Legal Basis and Ownership Structure
key_dimensions: Established under the National Housing Bank Act, 1987; commenced operations July 9, 1988
Originally a wholly-owned subsidiary of RBI; ownership transferred to Government of India in 2019
Distinction: NHB is NOT a scheduled bank but a statutory development finance institution
UPSC trap: Confusing NHB's parent body as RBI (pre-2019) vs. GoI (post-2019)

concepts.name: NHB's Regulatory Role over Housing Finance Companies (HFCs)
key_dimensions: NHB was the primary regulator of HFCs until 2019; regulatory authority transferred to RBI via Finance Act 2019
NHB retains refinancing and promotional functions even after losing regulatory role
UPSC trap: Assuming NHB still regulates HFCs — it does NOT post-2019
Distinction between NHB as regulator vs. RBI as current regulator of HFCs

concepts.name: Objectives and Mandate of NHB: The Three-Pillar Framework
key_dimensions: Three core functions: Regulation (erstwhile), Refinancing, and Promotion/Development
Mandate to promote a sound, healthy, viable and cost-effective housing finance system
Focus on augmenting resources for the housing sector and making housing credit accessible
Special emphasis on underserved segments: rural housing, EWS, LIG categories

concepts.name: NHB's Refinancing Operations: Mechanism and Eligible Institutions
key_dimensions: NHB provides refinance to Scheduled Commercial Banks, HFCs, Cooperative Banks, RRBs, and Apex Cooperative Housing Finance Societies
Refinance is provided against housing loans extended by these institutions — not direct lending to borrowers
UPSC trap: NHB does NOT directly lend to individuals; it is a second-tier/apex institution
Distinction between NHB refinance and direct retail housing loans by banks

concepts.name: NHB and the RESIDEX: India's Housing Price Index
key_dimensions: NHB launched RESIDEX in 2007 — India's first official residential property price index
Tracks residential property price movements across cities on a quarterly basis
Relevance: Used as a benchmark for policy, lending decisions, and inflation assessment in real estate
UPSC trap: Distinguishing RESIDEX (NHB) from other indices like RBI's House Price Index or CREDAI indices

concepts.name: NHB and Affordable Housing: Schemes and Priority Sector Linkage
key_dimensions: NHB channels funds under PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana) as a Central Nodal Agency (CNA)
Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) routed through NHB for EWS/LIG/MIG categories
NHB acts as one of the three CNAs along with HUDCO and SBI for PMAY-Urban
UPSC trap: NHB is NOT the sole nodal agency under PMAY; multiple CNAs exist

concepts.name: Rural Housing Fund (RHF) and NHB
key_dimensions: RHF established with NHB to provide refinance to eligible institutions for rural housing loans
Funded through shortfall contributions by scheduled commercial banks falling short of priority sector lending targets in rural housing
Parallel structure: RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund) with NABARD vs. RHF with NHB
UPSC trap: Confusing RHF (NHB) with RIDF (NABARD) — both funded by PSL shortfall but serve different purposes

concepts.name: Urban Housing Fund (UHF) and NHB
key_dimensions: UHF created with NHB to extend refinance for affordable urban housing, especially EWS and LIG
Funded through PSL shortfall contributions — similar mechanism to RHF but for urban housing
Distinction: RHF targets rural housing; UHF targets urban housing — both managed by NHB
UPSC trap: Assuming only NABARD manages PSL shortfall funds; NHB also manages RHF and UHF

concepts.name: NHB's Capital Structure and Funding Sources
key_dimensions: NHB raises resources through bonds, debentures, borrowings from RBI/GoI, and external borrowings (NHB bonds are eligible for SLR)
NHB bonds have been classified as eligible for SLR purposes — making them attractive to banks
UPSC angle: NHB bonds vs. regular corporate bonds — statutory backing and SLR eligibility
Distinction between NHB's liability-side (bonds) and asset-side (refinance loans) operations

concepts.name: Transfer of Regulatory Powers from NHB to RBI (Finance Act 2019)
key_dimensions: Finance Act 2019 amended the NHB Act, 1987 — RBI became the regulator of HFCs
Rationale: Greater systemic risk oversight after IL&FS and DHFL crises exposed gaps in NHB's regulatory capacity
NHB retained its promotional and refinancing role; only regulatory authority moved to RBI
UPSC trap: Believing NHB still has supervisory/regulatory jurisdiction over HFCs post-2019

concepts.name: NHB vs. HUDCO: Comparison of Mandates and Structures
key_dimensions: HUDCO (Housing and Urban Development Corporation): Government of India enterprise under MoHUA; focuses on project financing and urban infrastructure
NHB: Statutory institution under NHB Act 1987; focuses on refinancing and housing finance system development
HUDCO directly lends to state governments, ULBs, and housing boards; NHB does NOT directly lend to end borrowers
UPSC trap: Treating NHB and HUDCO as interchangeable — fundamentally different mandates, structures and lending models

concepts.name: NHB's Role in Securitization of Housing Loans
key_dimensions: NHB facilitates mortgage-backed securitization (MBS) to deepen the housing finance market
Provides liquidity to primary lending institutions by purchasing and securitizing mortgage pools
Distinction: NHB's MBS is a secondary market mechanism vs. primary lending by HFCs/banks
Relevance to priority sector: Securitized housing loan pools can be counted under PSL if they meet conditions

concepts.name: NHB and the Co-operative Housing Finance System
key_dimensions: NHB provides refinance to State Apex Cooperative Housing Finance Societies (SACHFs) and Primary Cooperative Housing Societies
Cooperative housing finance is a distinct track separate from commercial bank/HFC route
UPSC angle: NHB's reach extends beyond commercial institutions to cooperative sector — often overlooked
Distinction: NABARD supports agricultural cooperatives; NHB supports housing cooperatives

concepts.name: NHB's Governance: Board Composition and Accountability
key_dimensions: Managed by a Board of Directors; Chairman & Managing Director appointed by Central Government
Post-2019 transfer of ownership from RBI to GoI: NHB now accountable to Ministry of Finance
Statutory auditor appointed; accounts laid before Parliament annually — ensures legislative oversight
UPSC trap: Post-2019, NHB's CMD is no longer appointed by RBI but by the Central Government

concepts.name: Interest Subvention Schemes and NHB as Implementation Agency
key_dimensions: NHB implements interest subvention schemes for housing loans to targeted groups (rural households, disaster-affected areas)
Under PMAY-CLSS, subsidy is upfront and credited to borrower's loan account — NHB releases to Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs)
NHB monitors utilization, tracks beneficiaries, and reports to MoHUA/MoRD
UPSC trap: Confusing the roles of NHB (implementation/fund channeling) vs. ministry (policy design)

concepts.name: NHB and Financial Inclusion in Housing: EWS, LIG and MIG Focus
key_dimensions: NHB's mandate explicitly includes extending housing finance to economically weaker sections and low-income groups
Category definitions: EWS (annual income up to ₹3 lakh), LIG (₹3–6 lakh), MIG-I (₹6–12 lakh), MIG-II (₹12–18 lakh) under PMAY
NHB designs refinance products with concessional rates to incentivize PLIs to lend to EWS/LIG
UPSC angle: Financial inclusion in housing credit is distinct from financial inclusion in deposit/savings context

concepts.name: NHB's Promotional and Developmental Functions Beyond Refinancing
key_dimensions: Conducts research, training, and capacity building for the housing finance sector
Publishes reports on housing finance trends, RESIDEX data, and HFC sector performance
Provides technical assistance to state governments for housing finance policy formulation
UPSC angle: NHB's 'soft' developmental role is often tested to distinguish it from purely credit-focused institutions

concepts.name: IL&FS and DHFL Crisis: Impact on NHB's Regulatory Credibility
key_dimensions: IL&FS (2018) and DHFL (2019) collapse exposed systemic risks in NBFC/HFC sector under NHB's oversight
These crises triggered the policy decision to transfer HFC regulation to RBI via Finance Act 2019
Lessons: Need for integrated financial sector regulation; gaps in NHB's supervisory capacity
UPSC angle: Regulatory arbitrage between banking (RBI-regulated) and HFC (NHB-regulated) sectors as a root cause

concepts.name: Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and Housing: NHB's Connecting Role
key_dimensions: Housing loans form part of PSL targets for scheduled commercial banks; NHB refinancing supports PSL compliance
PSL shortfall in housing sub-target is channeled into RHF/UHF managed by NHB
Specific PSL housing limits: Loans up to ₹35 lakh in metros (population ≥10 lakh) qualify; lower caps in other areas
UPSC trap: Not all housing loans qualify for PSL — loan size and location-based caps apply; NHB refinance ≠ automatic PSL classification

concepts.name: Distinction: NHB Act 1987 vs. SARFAESI Act — NHB's Role in Mortgage Recovery
key_dimensions: SARFAESI Act 2002 empowers banks and HFCs to enforce security interest without court intervention — NHB itself is NOT a direct enforcer
NHB supports the legal framework that enables HFCs/banks to recover mortgage loans efficiently
Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest (CERSAI) — NHB is a stakeholder but not the managing body
UPSC trap: Conflating NHB's refinancing role with direct mortgage enforcement powers under SARFAESI
